title: Claude Code skills vs subagents: the shared simulator bug
summary: Óscar Gallego describes false UI-test failures when Rydger’s agents share a Simulator, then assigns devices per worktree and gives only one reviewer ownership of test execution. An iOS team can inventory shared resources before parallelizing; his private-project account reports five clean runs of 35 tests, but lacks a measured baseline failure rate or token-cost comparison.
takeaway: Isolate Simulators and generated state per worktree, keep read-only reviews parallel, and assign test execution explicitly so reviewers do not disrupt each other.
